description:
Derived data and results of the paper Class Imbalance and Domain Shift in Vehicle Dynamics-Based Driver Drowsiness Detection (Nakagama, Ishii, Yoshizoe). The paper evaluates a random-forest driver drowsiness detector built on vehicle-dynamics features in a full factorial experiment over four design factors — rebalancing method (7 levels), training mode (Cross/Within/Mixed), inter-subject distance metric (MMD/DTW/W1) and subject group (In/Out) — replicated with 12 random seeds (126 factor cells, 1,512 evaluations).

Contents. (1) data/processed/common/ — per-subject-session feature tables (vehicle-dynamics window features, EEG band powers used to derive the labels, and the drowsiness labels) for the 87 subject-sessions. (2) results/analysis/exp2_domain_shift/ — the metric tables of the 1,512 evaluations, the tables derived from them (performance per rebalancing method and training mode, Sobol sensitivity indices), the inter-subject distance matrices and In/Out subject lists, and the figures of the paper.

Trained model binaries are not included: they require an exact dependency-version match to load and carry arbitrary-code-execution risk on unpickling. They can be retrained with the code repository.

Provenance. All measurements derive from the multi-modal driving dataset of Aygun et al. (2024), Harvard Dataverse, doi:10.7910/DVN/HMZ5RG, released under CC0 1.0. This record redistributes only derived features and analysis outputs, not the upstream raw recordings. Please cite the upstream deposit alongside this record.

Documentation. DATADICTIONARY.md describes every file and column; MANIFEST.sha256 and BUNDLE_INFO.json record per-file checksums and the source commit of the code repository.

Licensing. Data and figures: CC BY 4.0. The accompanying source code is released under the MIT License (see LICENSE).
references: Aygun, A.; Blaney, G.; Haga, Z.; McWilliams, T.; Mertens, J.; de Ruiter, J. P.; Ward, N.; Scheutz, M. Multi-modal data acquisition platform for behavioral evaluation. Harvard Dataverse, 2024. DOI: 10.7910/DVN/HMZ5RG

Aygun, A.; Blaney, G.; Haga, Z.; McWilliams, T.; Mertens, J.; de Ruiter, J. P.; Ward, N.; Scheutz, M. A multimodal virtual reality data acquisition platform and dataset to assess systemic human cognitive states. Scientific Data, 13(1):76, 2026.
notes: The In/Out grouping (split2) is at subject-session level: the 87 subject-sessions come from 47 drivers, and a driver with two sessions can have one session in each group. The per-group lists ship with the bundle. The upstream deposit doi:10.7910/DVN/HMZ5RG is released under CC0 1.0; please cite it in addition to this record.
